lesson_title: The Wheel That Makes Things Nod
hook_text: Spin a wheel and something bobs up and down. That is a cam, and it is inside your car, your sewing machine and a wooden giraffe.
clip_script: Here is a wheel that turns spinning into bobbing. Put a disc on a shaft, but drill the hole off centre. Rest a rod on top. Spin it. The far side pushes the rod up, the near side lets it fall. Round and round became up and down. That is a cam, and the rod is the follower. The off-centre disc is the eccentric wheel: smooth, even, like a wave. Now change the shape to a snail shell: a spiral that grows and then drops at a step. The follower climbs slowly, then falls in an instant. That is a snail cam, and it only turns one way. Gentle nodding giraffe: eccentric. Tapping woodpecker: snail. Car engine valves: cams opening and closing hundreds of times a second. One spinning shaft, any motion you like.
visual_style: Whiteboard disc with an off-centre dot spins under a vertical rod that bobs; the disc morphs into a spiral with a step and the rod climbs then drops; a giraffe and a woodpecker silhouette appear.
pacing: Eccentric demonstration, snail demonstration, three everyday uses, one-line summary.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch both cams with their followers and arrows.
